_meta.note: Shareable snapshot. IC client detail and GoodUI member data removed. Third-party results are benchmarks from public case studies, not the library owner's own results.

ideas.title: Installment price line beside the main price
ideas.hypothesis: If the installment amount (e.g. '4 x $30') sits beside the full price at the price moment, then CVR rises, because affordability is judged at the point the price is read, not at checkout.
ideas.run_when: AOV over about $80 and an installment provider is live
ideas.do_not_run_when: installments unavailable or amounts not real
ideas.plain_english: Show the buy now pay later amount right next to the price.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when AOV is over about $80 and an installment provider is already live on site.

ideas.title: Installment amount as CTA microcopy
ideas.hypothesis: If the CTA carries the specific installment figure ('8 weekly payments of $12.38'), then transactions rise, because the specific number beats a generic benefit line at the click.
ideas.run_when: as above; beat HPA-29 benefit microcopy head to head
ideas.plain_english: Put the weekly or fortnightly payment amount into the button text.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when installments are live and the CTA currently carries a generic benefit line instead of the real figure.

ideas.title: Exit modal that surfaces installment pricing
ideas.hypothesis: If exiting visitors see the installment offer instead of a guarantee, then sales and revenue rise, because price is the dominant unstated objection.
ideas.plain_english: Show leaving visitors the installment offer instead of a guarantee.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when exit surveys or price objections suggest affordability, not risk, is the unstated reason people leave.

ideas.title: Exit modal that restates the guarantee
ideas.hypothesis: If exiting visitors see the guarantee, then CVR rises, because risk is the objection. (Lost head to head to the installment modal.)
ideas.plain_english: Show leaving visitors a reminder of the money back guarantee.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when research names risk or trust, not price, as the top reason visitors leave without buying.

ideas.title: Installment availability visible at the checkout price/payment step
ideas.hypothesis: If installment availability is visible above the fold at checkout (not requiring early selection), then checkout CVR and revenue rise, because surfacing availability is the driver, not the act of selecting a plan.
ideas.plain_english: Make installment payment availability visible at the top of checkout.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when installments exist but checkout hides them until a payment plan is actively selected.

ideas.title: Raise or lower list price
ideas.hypothesis: If list price moves, then RPV changes, because demand elasticity is unknown. (Three HPA attempts, all inconclusive; needs Track B window and orders-per-arm sizing.)
ideas.plain_english: Test selling at a higher or lower price.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only with a Track B window, orders per arm sizing, and client sign off on moving list price.

ideas.title: New-visitor first-order offer
ideas.hypothesis: If new visitors get a first-order offer, then CVR rises, because a reason to act now is added. (Inconclusive at HPA.)
ideas.plain_english: Give first time visitors an offer on their first order.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when new visitor conversion lags returning traffic badly and there is no reason to buy today.

ideas.title: Remove header/footer/back links from checkout
ideas.hypothesis: If navigation exits are removed from checkout, then checkout CVR rises, because every exit is an invitation to leave at the money moment.
ideas.plain_english: Remove menus and back links from the checkout pages.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when checkout analytics show exits back into the site from the payment steps.

ideas.title: Strip the confirmation-page header so order details sit above the fold
ideas.hypothesis: If the confirmation page loses its header, then follow-on revenue rises, because the order details and next action are seen immediately.
ideas.plain_english: Trim the confirmation page header so order details show immediately.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the confirmation page pushes order details and the next action below the fold.

ideas.title: Remove account creation or login before checkout
ideas.hypothesis: If the registration or login step before checkout is removed, then CVR rises, because a form between intent and payment is the costliest friction on the site.
ideas.plain_english: Let people buy without creating an account or logging in first.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a login or registration step sits between the cart and payment and drop off is heavy there.

ideas.title: Checkout pay-button label
ideas.hypothesis: If the pay CTA names the outcome ('Purchase course', 'Enroll') instead of a generic verb, then checkout CVR rises, because the label confirms what the click does.
ideas.plain_english: Change the checkout button to name what the buyer is getting.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the checkout button uses a generic verb rather than naming what the click actually buys.

ideas.title: Same upsell as an interstitial instead of inline
ideas.hypothesis: If the upsell interrupts as an interstitial, then it will NOT beat the inline placement, because interruptions lose to inline at the same intent moment (13 vs 25 sales).
ideas.plain_english: Show the same upsell as a pop up instead of on the page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only to confirm the inline placement wins; interruptive placement has already lost head to head.

ideas.title: Inline upsell below the checkout order summary
ideas.hypothesis: If an upgrade offer sits inline below the order summary, then revenue per order rises, because checkout is a peak-intent moment and the offer does not interrupt the flow.
ideas.plain_english: Add an upgrade offer under the order summary at checkout.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when checkout carries an obvious upgrade and the order summary has room without adding a step.

ideas.title: Bundle or package upsell block on the listing page
ideas.hypothesis: If the listing page promotes the bundle, then AOV rises, because the premium option becomes visible before the single-item choice is made. (Inconclusive twice at HPA.)
ideas.plain_english: Promote the bundle on the category page before shoppers pick one item.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a bundle exists but is only discoverable after the single item choice has been made.

ideas.title: Complementary-product bundle upsell under add-to-cart
ideas.hypothesis: If a complementary bundle is offered under ATC, then AOV rises; the bundle discount must not exceed the lift (SR-011: +35% ATC, RPV flat because the 10% discount absorbed it).
ideas.do_not_run_when: never lead with a discount; test full price first
ideas.plain_english: Offer a matching add on product just under the add to cart button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when order data shows a repeatable pairing; test at full price before adding any bundle discount.

ideas.title: Add a direct link to a money page in the main nav
ideas.hypothesis: If a money page (premium tier, category, sale, free entry) gets a main-nav link, then transactions rise, because the link advertises the page's existence even to people who never click it.
ideas.plain_english: Add a main menu link straight to an important money page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a high value page (premium tier, sale, category) has no link in the main menu.

ideas.title: Package/tier dropdown with a 'best value' or savings label
ideas.hypothesis: If tiers are listed in a nav dropdown with a value label ('SAVE UP TO 77%', 'best value'), then package purchases rise, because the premium option is made visible and framed.
ideas.plain_english: List the packages in the menu with a best value label.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when tiers or packages exist but the premium option is invisible until deep in the funnel.

ideas.title: Consolidate, hide, or restructure main navigation
ideas.hypothesis: If nav items are hidden or restructured, then CVR will most likely FALL, because heatmaps under-measure the passive value of nav links (HPA-178 -12% CVR, SR-004/SR-010 -10% CVR each).
ideas.run_when: only with tree-testing evidence and a Track B window
ideas.do_not_run_when: nav touch rate under 5%; heatmap-only justification
ideas.plain_english: Hide or restructure the main navigation menu.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only with tree testing evidence and a Track B window; heatmap only justification has lost three times.

ideas.title: Add breadcrumb navigation
ideas.hypothesis: If breadcrumbs are added, then CVR rises, because visitors can move sideways in the catalogue without the back button.
ideas.plain_english: Add breadcrumb links so shoppers can move sideways through the range.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when analytics show heavy back button use moving between categories and product pages.

ideas.title: Visible filter pills on the collection page
ideas.hypothesis: If collection filters are exposed as one-tap pills, then RPV rises, because match quality improves (primary must be CVR/RPV, not click-through).
ideas.run_when: Catalogue is large, filters exist, and replay or analytics show filter use with high abandonment.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Catalogue is small enough that filtering is never needed.
ideas.plain_english: Turn collection filters into one tap pills shoppers can see.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the catalogue is large, filters exist, and replay shows filter use with high abandonment.

ideas.title: Homepage hero message (what the fold says)
ideas.hypothesis: If the hero says one specific thing to the primary visitor (outcome or product), then transactions rise, because the fold's message, not its content volume, drives the decision.
ideas.plain_english: Make the homepage headline say one specific thing to the main visitor.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the homepage fold says several things at once and none of them names the outcome.

ideas.title: Move product/category panels into the first viewport
ideas.hypothesis: If the primary buying routes sit in the first viewport instead of below a decorative hero, then transactions rise, because the fold gets one job.
ideas.run_when: catalogue breadth; homepage entry share high
ideas.do_not_run_when: Single-product or very small catalogue.
ideas.plain_english: Move product and category panels up into the first screen.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when catalogue breadth matters and homepage entry share is high but products sit below a decorative hero.

ideas.title: USP card as slide 1 of the PDP gallery
ideas.hypothesis: If the first gallery slide is a USP card instead of a product photo, then CVR rises, because the key claim is read before the scroll. (Won; the reverse swap lost.)
ideas.plain_english: Make the first product image a card carrying the main selling point.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the key claim only appears in body copy and the gallery opens on a plain product shot.

ideas.title: Remove or demote the above-the-fold video
ideas.hypothesis: If the VSL/video is removed from or moved below the fold, then transactions rise, because big media has to earn its place and mostly does not.
ideas.plain_english: Remove the video from the top of the page or move it down.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a video or VSL occupies the fold and play rates do not justify the space.

ideas.title: Remove intro copy/banner so products show immediately
ideas.hypothesis: If the category intro block is stripped, then transactions rise, because products reach the first viewport. (Matches Evidoo's 17-test mobile PLP hero removal pattern.)
ideas.plain_english: Delete the category intro text so products appear straight away.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a category intro block or banner pushes products out of the first mobile viewport.

ideas.title: Restructure the PDP/sales page above the fold
ideas.hypothesis: If the ATF layout is redesigned (two-column, USP blocks, standardised sections), then CVR rises. (Eight HPA attempts, all inconclusive: addition-led redesigns do not move the number.)
ideas.do_not_run_when: redesign is addition-led; run a message or subtraction test instead
ideas.plain_english: Rebuild the top of the product or sales page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only after single element message and subtraction tests are exhausted; addition led redesigns have gone eight for zero.

ideas.title: Listing card layout and grid density
ideas.hypothesis: If listing cards are restructured (2-up mobile grid, merged ranges, cleaner panels), then PDP views and CVR rise, because more comparable products are visible per scroll.
ideas.plain_english: Change the product card layout and how many fit per row.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the mobile grid shows few products per scroll or cards are inconsistent and hard to compare.

ideas.title: Passive 'best suited for' labelling at the decision point
ideas.hypothesis: If a static 'best for' line sits on the card, the PDP, and the cart line item, then CVR and mix rise, because confident-but-wrong buyers get the answer without asking for it.
ideas.run_when: support tickets or returns show fit/choice confusion
ideas.plain_english: Add a short best suited for line on cards, product pages and cart.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when support tickets or returns show fit or model choice confusion.

ideas.title: Static comparison table across similar models
ideas.hypothesis: If similar models are compared in a static table, then ATC and CVR rise, because cross-PDP hopping is replaced by one view. (Hyperice +6.2% corroborates.)
ideas.run_when: multiple similar SKUs and research shows confusion
ideas.plain_english: Add a simple table comparing the similar models side by side.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when there are multiple similar models and research shows shoppers hopping between product pages to compare.

ideas.title: Fit / installation / placement FAQ on the PDP
ideas.hypothesis: If the top fit and installation questions are answered statically on the PDP, then mobile CVR rises, because the objection is cleared where it arises.
ideas.run_when: Fit or space uncertainty drives support tickets and returns, and the current answer lives off-site.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The section would add doubt above the buy decision, or the same accordion is already under test.
ideas.plain_english: Answer the top fit and installation questions on the product page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when fit or space uncertainty drives support tickets and returns and the answer currently lives off site.

ideas.title: Interactive sizing/help modal near the decision
ideas.hypothesis: If buyers are asked to open an interactive helper, then CVR will FALL, because interactive help introduces doubt and effort at the decision (-48% CVR).
ideas.do_not_run_when: never near the ATC
ideas.plain_english: Add an interactive sizing or help tool near the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Do not run near add to cart; the interactive helper lost 48 percent of conversions.

ideas.title: USP or warranty tooltips next to add-to-cart
ideas.hypothesis: If USPs are hidden behind tooltips near the CTA, then CVR will FALL, because hover/tap reassurance is not read and the warranty wording created the objection (-22.8%).
ideas.plain_english: Hide selling points behind hover tooltips beside the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Do not run; hidden tooltip reassurance is not read and the warranty wording created the objection.

ideas.title: 'Why this beats the alternative' objection section
ideas.hypothesis: If the page argues specifically why this beats the obvious alternative (online vs in-person, this rack vs a $30 hook), then CVR rises, because a specific objection answer is revenue while a generic trust badge is noise.
ideas.plain_english: Add a section arguing why this beats the obvious cheaper alternative.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when research names a specific competing alternative shoppers weigh the product against.

ideas.title: Specific benefit or guarantee microcopy under the CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If one specific line sits under the CTA ('Instant access. Lifetime updates.', warranty-specific wording), then CVR rises, because specific beats generic in every microcopy test.
ideas.plain_english: Add one specific reassurance line directly under the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the space under the CTA is empty or carries a generic reassurance line.

ideas.title: 'Talk to us' CTA beside buy on high-ticket items
ideas.hypothesis: If high-ticket pages offer a human contact path, then CVR rises, because some buyers need a conversation. (Inconclusive.)
ideas.plain_english: Add a talk to us option next to the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the item is high ticket, support gets pre purchase questions, and someone can staff the channel.

ideas.title: Generic trust or USP bar (sitewide or section)
ideas.hypothesis: If a generic USP/trust bar is added, then CVR will NOT move (or falls), because generic trust marquees assert rather than argue (SR-024 kill rule, HPA-21, SR-007, HPA-151).
ideas.run_when: Brand is unfamiliar to most traffic, or exit survey and support data show payment-security hesitation.
ideas.do_not_run_when: trust already scores high in research
ideas.plain_english: Add a row of generic trust or benefit icons across the site.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only when the brand is unfamiliar to most traffic or research shows payment security hesitation.

ideas.title: Reviews widget or prominent star rating on the PDP
ideas.hypothesis: If reviews are made prominent, then CVR rises modestly for new visitors at best; stars alone assert and lost at SR-018. Quote arguments, not ratings.
ideas.run_when: proof that argues (reasoned quotes)
ideas.do_not_run_when: stars-only prominence
ideas.plain_english: Make customer reviews more prominent on the product page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when reviews contain reasoned arguments worth quoting; stars only prominence has already lost.

ideas.title: Guarantee as a tooltip or modal
ideas.hypothesis: If the guarantee is placed behind a tooltip or modal, then CVR will not move, because interactive reassurance is not opened. Make it static text instead.
ideas.plain_english: Put the guarantee behind a tooltip or pop up instead of plain text.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only to prove the static version wins; interactive reassurance is not opened at the decision.

ideas.title: Offer stack / benefits list under the CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If a benefits/offer stack is listed under ATC, then CVR rises. (SR-015 3-arm lost; HPA accordions won when they replaced a wall of copy: subtraction, not addition.)
ideas.plain_english: List the offer and its benefits under the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run as a replacement for a wall of copy, not as an addition to an already crowded buy box.

ideas.title: Primary CTA label wording
ideas.hypothesis: If the primary CTA names the action outcome, then CVR rises, because the specific verb removes hesitation.
ideas.plain_english: Reword the main button so it names what happens next.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the main button uses a generic verb rather than naming the outcome of the click.

ideas.title: Sticky add-to-cart / buy CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If the CTA follows the scroll, then CVR rises, because the action is always one tap away. (Inconclusive on desktop at HPA; CRE sticky-CTA win report exists.)
ideas.run_when: long PDPs, mobile
ideas.plain_english: Keep the buy button visible as the page scrolls.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run on long product pages with heavy mobile traffic where the CTA scrolls out of reach.

ideas.title: 'See pricing' jump link above the fold
ideas.hypothesis: If a jump-to-pricing link sits in the fold, then CVR rises, because price-first visitors get there without scrolling. (Inconclusive.)
ideas.plain_english: Add a jump link at the top that scrolls straight to pricing.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when price sits far below the fold and scroll data shows visitors hunting for it.

ideas.title: Remove a choice before add-to-cart (combine options)
ideas.hypothesis: If two options are combined into one package so the buyer makes one fewer choice, then purchases rise (+41% at 96%), because choice at the money moment is friction.
ideas.plain_english: Combine two buying choices into one so there is less to decide.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when buyers face two separate choices before add to cart that could honestly be one package.

ideas.title: Remove secondary CTAs from listing cards
ideas.hypothesis: If the extra CTA on each card is removed, then PDP views and CVR rise, because one action per card. (Inconclusive.)
ideas.run_when: Click data shows one hero path taking the large majority of clicks and the other paths are minority routes.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The secondary path carries material click volume or revenue, or the click split has not been measured first.
ideas.plain_english: Remove the extra button from each product card.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when click data shows one hero path taking the large majority of clicks on each card.

ideas.title: Search results page redesign
ideas.hypothesis: If search results are restructured, then CVR for searchers rises. (HPA win, no verbatim number.)
ideas.plain_english: Rebuild the search results page layout.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when internal search carries meaningful sessions and searchers convert above average.

ideas.title: Campaign or product-specific landing page
ideas.hypothesis: If a campaign gets a dedicated page matched to its message, then CVR rises, because message match. (Mixed at HPA.)
ideas.plain_english: Build a dedicated page matched to a specific campaign or product.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a campaign sends real volume to a generic page whose message does not match the ad.

ideas.title: Free-shipping threshold vs flat rate (and threshold level)
ideas.hypothesis: If shipping is framed as free over a threshold vs flat rate, then RPV changes with the threshold-to-AOV ratio; the offer must be genuinely attractive (Sport Chek reversal at $75).
ideas.run_when: threshold near median order value; most orders naturally qualify
ideas.do_not_run_when: threshold well above AOV
ideas.plain_english: Change shipping from a flat rate to free over a spend threshold.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the shipping threshold sits near median order value and most orders naturally qualify.

ideas.title: Remove or hide the coupon field at checkout
ideas.hypothesis: If the open coupon field is removed or collapsed behind a link, then checkout CVR rises, because an empty coupon box advertises a discount the visitor does not have and sends them hunting.
ideas.plain_english: Hide the discount code box behind a link at checkout.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when an empty coupon box sits open at checkout and exit data shows code hunting.

ideas.title: Text labels on icons
ideas.hypothesis: If icons carry a text label, then engagement and CVR rise, because unlabeled icons are guessed, not read.
ideas.plain_english: Add text labels beside the icons.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when header or interface icons carry no text label and click data shows they are missed.

ideas.title: Fewer form fields
ideas.hypothesis: If optional fields are removed from the form, then completion rises, because every field is a cost paid before the reward.
ideas.plain_english: Cut the optional fields out of the form.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the form asks for anything beyond what is needed to ship and charge.

ideas.title: Form field layout, labels, sizing and helpers
ideas.hypothesis: If field labels sit above the field, stay visible (no floating labels), fields are larger and single-column with explanations only where needed, then completion rises, because the form is read faster and errors fall. (Floating labels: Evidoo 0/8 wins.)
ideas.run_when: Checkout asks for anything beyond the minimum needed to ship and charge.
ideas.do_not_run_when: floating labels on mobile
ideas.plain_english: Fix the form layout: visible labels, bigger fields, one column.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when checkout uses floating labels, cramped fields or multi column layouts, especially on mobile.

ideas.title: Form step order, step count, progress indication
ideas.hypothesis: If easy fields come first, steps are split or merged to match commitment, and progress is shown, then completion rises, because early momentum carries the harder asks.
ideas.plain_english: Reorder the form steps and show progress through them.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when form completion drops sharply at one step and there is no progress indication.

ideas.title: Ask for payment before account or details
ideas.hypothesis: If payment is the first step and details follow, then purchases rise, because the commitment is captured while intent is highest.
ideas.plain_english: Take payment first and collect the remaining details after.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the platform allows payment first and details collection is currently front loaded.

ideas.title: Exposed menu options instead of a hamburger
ideas.hypothesis: If top categories are exposed instead of hidden behind a hamburger, then product-page reach and CVR rise, because a visible path advertises the catalogue (Ferplast +32%).
ideas.plain_english: Show the top menu categories instead of hiding them behind a menu icon.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when top categories are hidden behind a hamburger and product page reach from the homepage is low.

ideas.title: Partial welcome mat / promo on entry
ideas.hypothesis: If an entry promo occupies part of the viewport (not full screen), then CVR rises, because the offer is seen without blocking the page.
ideas.plain_english: Show a partial screen promo when visitors arrive.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when there is a genuine standing offer and no entry promo currently exists on the homepage.

ideas.title: Sort order: least or most expensive first
ideas.hypothesis: If the default sort anchors on the higher price first, then RPV rises, because later prices read as cheaper. (Mixed; run with RPV primary.)
ideas.plain_english: Change whether the cheapest or most expensive products show first.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run with revenue per visitor as the primary metric; conversion rate alone will mislead on price sorting.

ideas.title: Specific customer or ownership count
ideas.hypothesis: If one specific count sits at the decision ('Trusted in 1M+ garages'), then CVR rises, because a specific number argues where a generic badge asserts.
ideas.plain_english: Add one specific customer count near the buy decision.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the brand has a real, verifiable customer or usage number that is currently unstated.

ideas.title: Anchor the price against what it protects or replaces
ideas.hypothesis: If the price is framed against the value at stake ('protects a $2,000 bike', 'what it's worth'), then CVR rises, because the reference point changes.
ideas.plain_english: Compare the price to the value of what the product protects.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the product protects or replaces something with a known and much larger value.

ideas.title: Inline link nudge within content
ideas.hypothesis: If a contextual link sits inside the content body, then click-through to the money page rises, because it appears at the moment of relevance.
ideas.plain_english: Add a contextual link inside the article body.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when content pages carry traffic but link out to money pages only from the navigation.

ideas.title: Visible stock availability
ideas.hypothesis: If real stock status is visible ('In stock', 'Only 3 left'), then CVR rises, because availability is an unstated question and low stock is honest urgency.
ideas.run_when: stock data is real
ideas.do_not_run_when: fabricated scarcity
ideas.plain_english: Show real stock levels on the product page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only where inventory data is real and live; never fabricate scarcity.

ideas.title: Specific delivery promise near the CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If a specific dispatch/delivery promise sits near ATC ('Order by 2pm, ships today, 2-5 days'), then CVR rises, because the vague range is a dread cost (CRE Diamondback +22%).
ideas.run_when: ops can honour it
ideas.plain_english: State a specific dispatch and delivery promise near the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when delivery timing is vague on the page and operations can honour a specific promise.

ideas.title: Repeat the CTA at the bottom of the page
ideas.hypothesis: If the CTA is repeated after the last content block, then CVR rises, because readers who scroll to the end are the most convinced and should not scroll back.
ideas.plain_english: Repeat the buy button at the bottom of the page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run on long pages where the only buy button sits at the top and scroll depth is good.

ideas.title: Cart reminder and recently viewed for returning visitors
ideas.hypothesis: If returning visitors with a basket or browse history see a delayed reminder or recently-viewed row, then transactions rise, because context is restored (Evidoo 6/6 wins +4.9%; Stone Creek +13% RPV).
ideas.run_when: persistent cart and returning traffic
ideas.plain_english: Remind returning visitors what is in their basket or what they viewed.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the cart persists and returning visitors are a meaningful share of sessions.

ideas.title: Surface content hidden behind tabs, accordions or clicks
ideas.hypothesis: If decision-relevant content (Q&A, specs, reviews) is shown inline instead of behind a tab, then CVR rises, because passive beats interactive.
ideas.plain_english: Show content inline instead of hiding it behind tabs.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when decision relevant content sits behind tabs or accordions and click data shows they are rarely opened.

ideas.title: Product photography treatment (authentic vs stock, single focus, thumbnails)
ideas.hypothesis: If product photos are authentic, single-focus and easy to browse, then CVR rises, because the photo does the comprehension work copy cannot.
ideas.plain_english: Use authentic, single focus product photos that are easy to browse.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when product photography is stock, cluttered or inconsistent across the range.

ideas.title: Open product pages in a new tab from listings
ideas.hypothesis: If listing clicks open in a new tab, then multi-product browsing and CVR change; mixed evidence, run as a listing-behaviour test.
ideas.plain_english: Open product pages in a new tab from the listing.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when shoppers compare several products and analytics show heavy back and forth between listings.

ideas.title: Size reference imagery
ideas.hypothesis: If product size is shown against a familiar reference, then CVR rises and returns fall, because 'will it fit' is answered passively.
ideas.run_when: fit/size is a stated barrier
ideas.plain_english: Show the product next to something familiar so size is obvious.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when fit or size is a stated barrier in research, support tickets or returns.

ideas.title: Countdown timer on a real deadline
ideas.hypothesis: If a real deadline is shown as a countdown, then CVR rises, because deferral has a visible cost. Only where the deadline is true.
ideas.run_when: genuine deadline
ideas.do_not_run_when: fake or resetting timers
ideas.plain_english: Show a countdown to a real deadline.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only where a genuine deadline exists; never use fake or resetting timers.

ideas.title: Longer, descriptive product titles
ideas.hypothesis: If titles carry the key attribute ('Wall-mount vertical bike rack, up to 55kg'), then CVR rises, because the title answers the first question (CRE Optibac titles).
ideas.plain_english: Add the key attribute into the product title.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when listing titles are short brand names that do not answer the shopper's first question.

ideas.title: Primary CTA in the first viewport
ideas.hypothesis: If the primary CTA is visible without scrolling, then CVR rises, because the action is available at the moment of intent.
ideas.plain_english: Move the main buy button into the first screen.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the buy button sits below the fold on the main template, especially on mobile.

ideas.title: Quick-add or shortcut buttons on listing cards
ideas.hypothesis: If listing cards carry a one-tap add or shortcut, then orders rise for low-consideration SKUs, because the PDP step is skipped.
ideas.run_when: low-consideration, repeat-buy catalogue
ideas.plain_english: Add a one tap add to cart button on listing cards.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the catalogue is low consideration and repeat buy and shoppers know what they want.

ideas.title: 'How it works' explainer section
ideas.hypothesis: If a short how-it-works block sits before the buy decision, then CVR rises for novel products, because the mechanism is understood before the price is judged.
ideas.plain_english: Add a short how it works section before the buy decision.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the product is novel and research shows visitors do not understand how it works.

ideas.title: Remove the full-height hero false bottom
ideas.hypothesis: If the hero no longer fills the viewport, then scroll depth and CVR rise, because visitors discover the persuasive content below (CRE iFLY +36%, Party Hard +5%).
ideas.plain_english: Stop the hero filling the whole screen so content below is discovered.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the hero fills the whole viewport and scroll depth data shows visitors stopping there.

ideas.title: Button and visual styling (filled vs ghost, shape, contrast, fonts)
ideas.hypothesis: If primary actions are filled, high-contrast and consistent, then CVR rises marginally, because affordance is clearer. Small effects; test last.
ideas.plain_english: Make the main buttons filled, high contrast and consistent.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run last, after message and structure tests; expect small effects.

ideas.title: Show currency and taxes before checkout
ideas.hypothesis: If the local currency and tax-inclusive total are shown before checkout, then checkout completion rises, because surprise costs are the top abandonment reason.
ideas.plain_english: Show local currency and tax inclusive totals before checkout.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when shoppers from other markets see prices in the wrong currency or tax exclusive.

ideas.title: Auto-apply the discount instead of a code field
ideas.hypothesis: If an eligible discount is applied automatically, then CVR rises, because the visitor neither hunts for a code nor doubts the price.
ideas.plain_english: Apply the eligible discount automatically instead of asking for a code.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when an eligible discount exists but shoppers must find and enter a code to get it.

ideas.title: Personalised next step on the confirmation page
ideas.hypothesis: If the confirmation page offers one relevant next action, then follow-on revenue rises, because post-purchase intent is at its peak.
ideas.plain_english: Offer one relevant next step on the order confirmation page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the confirmation page carries no next action and repeat purchase is real in the category.

ideas.title: Priming or quiz step before the listing
ideas.hypothesis: If a short priming step routes the visitor to a matched subset, then CVR rises, because choice is reduced and commitment begins. (SR quiz popup exists; weak evidence.)
ideas.plain_english: Add a short quiz that routes shoppers to matching products.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the range is broad and research shows shoppers do not know where to start.

ideas.title: Copy personalised to traffic source or location
ideas.hypothesis: If the headline or proof matches the visitor's source or location, then CVR rises, because message match. Few tests.
ideas.plain_english: Change the headline to match where the visitor came from.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when paid campaigns send distinct audiences to one generic page.

ideas.title: Badges and structured info on cards ('Most popular', attributes)
ideas.hypothesis: If cards carry a small number of meaningful badges, then CVR rises, because the default choice is signalled. Too many badges cancel out.
ideas.plain_english: Add a small number of meaningful badges to product cards.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when cards carry no signal of which product is the popular or default choice.

ideas.title: Onboarding callouts / tooltips on first visit
ideas.hypothesis: If callouts explain the interface, then CVR will not rise (GoodUI meta -1.7%), because interruptions cost more than they teach.
ideas.plain_english: Show first time visitors tooltips explaining the interface.
ideas.ideation_hint: Do not run; interface callouts cost more attention than they teach.

ideas.title: Preselect the recommended option / quantity / plan
ideas.hypothesis: If the recommended option is preselected and labelled, then RPV rises, because the default is taken by the undecided (GoodUI meta +5.5%; HPA 'best value' +73%).
ideas.run_when: the default is genuinely the best fit for most
ideas.do_not_run_when: the default pushes the priciest option regardless of fit
ideas.plain_english: Preselect the recommended option and label why it is recommended.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the default is genuinely the best fit for most buyers, not just the priciest.

ideas.title: Auto-advance after each selection in a configurator
ideas.hypothesis: If the next step opens automatically after a selection, then completion rises slightly, because one click is removed per step.
ideas.plain_english: Open the next step automatically after each choice is made.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a multi step configurator shows drop off between selection steps.

ideas.title: Visible search field instead of an icon
ideas.hypothesis: If the search field is exposed, then search use and CVR rise where searchers convert above average (USA Containers +13% CVR at 80% sig).
ideas.run_when: search users convert well but usage is low
ideas.plain_english: Show the search box instead of a search icon.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when search users convert above average but search usage is low and hidden behind an icon.

ideas.title: Static guarantee or returns statement near the CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If the guarantee or returns window is stated as plain text at the decision, then CVR rises, because risk is answered passively (vs tooltips/modals which are not opened).
ideas.plain_english: State the guarantee as plain text next to the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the guarantee or returns policy is only reachable from the footer or a modal.

ideas.title: Carousel vs static image grid
ideas.hypothesis: If carousels are replaced by a static grid, then CVR rises, because slides after the first are rarely seen (CRE Mobbin).
ideas.plain_english: Replace the carousel with a static grid of images.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when carousel analytics show slides after the first are rarely seen.

ideas.title: Price framing and format (per-unit, per-day, one-time, superscript)
ideas.hypothesis: If the price is framed in the smallest honest unit and formatted cleanly, then CVR rises, because the perceived cost drops without a discount.
ideas.plain_english: Show the price in the smallest honest unit.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the price can honestly be expressed per unit, per day or per serve.

ideas.title: How visible the price is before the decision
ideas.hypothesis: If price visibility changes (earlier vs later), then CVR changes with price competitiveness; show early when price is a strength.
ideas.plain_english: Change how early the price is shown in the journey.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when price is a competitive strength and currently sits late in the journey.

ideas.title: Product description length and structure
ideas.hypothesis: If the description leads with the buyer's decision variables in scannable form, then CVR rises, because the description is read for an answer, not a story.
ideas.plain_english: Rewrite the description to lead with what buyers actually decide on.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when descriptions are long prose and research shows buyers hunting for specific answers.

ideas.title: Static proof or objection-clearing line in the cart after add-to-cart
ideas.hypothesis: If a static line under the cart line item confirms the choice with a specific number (an aggregate rating, or the stat that answers the top pre-purchase objection), then checkout-begin rate rises, because the doubt that surfaces in the seconds after add-to-cart is answered where it happens rather than back on the product page.
ideas.run_when: Cart or drawer is bare (line item plus checkout button), ATC-to-checkout is the funnel's biggest leak, and research names either a dominant objection or a strong verifiable rating.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The cart already carries several reassurance blocks, or the stat cannot be substantiated from real review or survey data.
ideas.plain_english: Add one reassuring line with a real number inside the cart.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the cart is bare and add to cart to checkout is the funnel's biggest leak.

ideas.title: Reason-why block that justifies the price premium inside the buy box
ideas.hypothesis: If three specific reasons the product costs more than the cheap category alternative sit directly under the price, then CVR rises, because the price objection is met with substantiation at the moment the number is read instead of being left to copy below the fold.
ideas.run_when: Price is the top stated barrier, the product is premium against a visibly cheaper alternative, and the buy box has vertical room.
ideas.do_not_run_when: A below-fold reason-why or comparison test is already running on the same page, or the product competes on price rather than quality.
ideas.plain_english: Give three specific reasons for the price, right under the price.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when price is the top stated barrier and the product is premium against a visibly cheaper option.

ideas.title: Full-price presentation instead of a permanent discount
ideas.hypothesis: If the always-on strikethrough and savings badges are removed and products show at full price, then RPV holds or rises, because a perpetual discount trains shoppers to wait for a better sale and undercuts the quality story that actually drives the purchase.
ideas.run_when: A discount has run continuously for months, survey data shows non-buyers waiting for a sale, and quality is the top persuasion driver.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Peak promotional trading, or the client cannot hold the change steady for a full Track B window.
ideas.plain_english: Sell at full price instead of a permanent discount.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a discount has run for months, buyers say they are waiting for a sale, and quality drives the purchase.

ideas.title: Quantity presets with a recommended option instead of a bare stepper
ideas.hypothesis: If the quantity control becomes a small set of preset options with a 'most popular' label and per-unit pricing shown, then AOV rises, because most buyers need more than one unit and a preset makes the multi-unit purchase the default mental model rather than a basket-total shock.
ideas.run_when: Research shows a majority of buyers need multiple units and no multi-unit offer exists anywhere on the site.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The product is genuinely a single-unit purchase, or a quantity discount ladder is already live on the same page.
ideas.plain_english: Replace the quantity box with preset options and a popular pick.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when research shows most buyers need several units and no multi unit offer exists.

ideas.title: Free gift at a quantity or spend threshold instead of a discount
ideas.hypothesis: If a small free accessory is offered at a multi-unit or spend threshold instead of a percentage discount, then RPV rises, because a free item carries disproportionate perceived value while a percentage discount hands margin back on every order that would have converted anyway.
ideas.run_when: Multi-unit demand exists, margin is thin, and a prior percentage-discount test ate its own conversion gain.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Fulfilment cannot reliably bundle the gift, or gift stock is constrained.
ideas.plain_english: Give a free small item at a spend threshold instead of a discount.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when multi unit demand exists, margin is thin, and a percentage discount has already eaten its own gain.

ideas.title: Social-norm line that makes buying more than one the normal choice
ideas.hypothesis: If a static line near add-to-cart states what most comparable customers actually buy, then AOV rises, because purchase quantity is set by an assumed norm, and the norm can be raised with proof instead of with margin.
ideas.run_when: Review attributes or survey data show most comparable households buy multiple units, and the client wants no offer mechanics.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The claim is not supported by the real order mix or the review corpus.
ideas.plain_english: Say what most similar customers actually buy, near the buy button.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only when the real order mix or review corpus supports the claim about what most customers buy.

ideas.title: Answered customer questions rendered on the page instead of behind a tab
ideas.hypothesis: If the top answered customer questions are rendered as a static on-page block, then CVR rises, because real objections in customer language with a staff answer deliver comprehension and proof at once, and a tab hides them from exactly the people who need them.
ideas.run_when: A review platform already holds answered questions behind a tab and objections are known to go unresolved at the decision point.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Another test occupies the same accordion or content region, or the existing answers are thin, stale, or off-topic.
ideas.plain_english: Show real answered customer questions on the page instead of in a tab.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a review platform already holds answered questions behind a tab and objections go unresolved.

ideas.title: Nudge from the entry model to the better-fitting model at the spec that disqualifies it
ideas.hypothesis: If the entry-level product page names the buyers it does not suit and points them to the model that does, right where the limiting spec appears, then RPV rises through mix shift, because shoppers who would have bought the wrong product or bounced are routed to the one that fits.
ideas.run_when: A high-traffic entry model carries specs that disqualify a known segment and the upgrade is only mentioned at the page bottom, and mix shift has previously produced verified revenue.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The upgrade model is out of stock, materially harder to fulfil, or lower margin.
ideas.plain_english: Tell entry model shoppers who it does not suit and point to the right one.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a high traffic entry model has specs that disqualify a known segment, mentioned only at page bottom.

ideas.title: Motion demo of the product's key mechanism on the listing card
ideas.hypothesis: If the first listing-card image becomes a lightweight animation of the product's differentiating mechanism, then CVR rises, because the feature that persuades is currently discovered too late in the funnel, and motion communicates it before the click without asking anyone to press play.
ideas.run_when: A mechanical or motion-based feature is a top persuasion driver but is only visible deep inside the PDP, and the page-weight budget allows a small animated asset.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Another test occupies the same collection surface, or the asset cannot be kept small enough to hold page speed.
ideas.plain_english: Make the first listing image a short animation of the key feature.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a motion based feature persuades but is only visible deep inside the product page.

ideas.title: Before-and-after outcome imagery in place of an early detail section
ideas.hypothesis: If an early homepage section doing detail-level work is replaced with a before-and-after image of the outcome, then CVR rises, because the transformation has to land before detail questions mean anything to a first-time visitor.
ideas.run_when: An FAQ or spec section sits high on the homepage ahead of the value proposition, and the outcome is genuinely visual.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The early section answers a documented entry objection that currently blocks progression.
ideas.plain_english: Replace an early detail section with a before and after image.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a detail or FAQ section sits high on the homepage ahead of the value proposition.

ideas.title: Replace brand-voice copy with the specific evidence behind the claim
ideas.hypothesis: If a self-congratulatory brand block is rewritten as the specific facts behind the quality claim (patents, units sold, test standards, where it is engineered), then CVR rises, because method marketing substantiates the attribute buyers say persuades them while brand adjectives do not.
ideas.run_when: Quality, craftsmanship or trust is the top stated persuasion driver and the site asserts it without evidence.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The supporting facts cannot be verified by the client, or the claims risk overstating the product.
ideas.plain_english: Replace brand adjectives with the specific facts behind the claim.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when quality or craftsmanship is the top stated driver but the site asserts it without evidence.

ideas.title: Emotional hero content instead of a functional search/booking form as the first element
ideas.hypothesis: If the first viewport leads with desire-building imagery and a single-field entry point instead of a dominant multi-field search form, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows visitors arriving in an exploration mindset convert better when given a reason to care before being asked to do work.
ideas.run_when: Homepage or category entry is dominated by a search/configurator form, entry-page bounce is high, and qualitative research says visitors arrive browsing rather than with a specific item in mind.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Traffic is predominantly high-intent repeat buyers who use search as their primary path, or search is the only viable way to navigate the catalogue.
ideas.plain_english: Lead the first screen with desire building imagery instead of a big search form.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a big search or configurator form dominates entry, bounce is high, and research says visitors arrive browsing.

ideas.title: Restyle the site's visual tone (palette, density, accreditation and review placement) to read as credible
ideas.hypothesis: If the site's visual tone is calmed and accreditation, reviews and price explanation are built into the design, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows aggressive or loud styling is read as untrustworthy on high-consideration purchases.
ideas.run_when: Survey or user testing scores the site low on trustworthiness, or a rebrand coincided with a conversion drop, and the offer is high-consideration or unusually cheap for its category.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Trust is not a stated barrier in research, or the brand is already well known to the visitor base.
ideas.plain_english: Calm the site's visual styling so it reads as credible.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when research scores the site low on trustworthiness, or a rebrand coincided with a conversion drop.

ideas.title: Show the actual product or result in use (screenshot, blurred result) instead of abstract illustration
ideas.hypothesis: If abstract illustration is replaced with imagery of the real product or the visitor's pending result, then lead or conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows future pacing closes the abstraction gap and makes the outcome feel imminent.
ideas.run_when: The page leans on illustration, icons or stock art, and research says visitors do not understand what they actually get.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The real product is visually unimpressive or not yet built, or imagery would overstate what the buyer receives.
ideas.plain_english: Show the real product or the real result instead of illustrations.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the page leans on illustration or stock art and research says visitors misunderstand what they get.

ideas.title: State the official/authorised relationship to the brand being sold, in the highest-traffic position
ideas.hypothesis: If the header states the specific official relationship to the brand on the page ('The official stockist of X'), then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows visitors who do not know they are on an authorised source hesitate at the buy decision.
ideas.run_when: The store resells or distributes named third-party brands and research shows visitors question legitimacy or assume a marketplace reseller.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The claim is not literally true, or the site is the brand's own single-brand store where the relationship is obvious.
ideas.plain_english: State in the header that you are the official stockist for the brand.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the store resells named brands and research shows visitors questioning legitimacy.

ideas.title: Structured 'what to do next' block at the end of articles with commitment-graduated options
ideas.hypothesis: If articles end with an explicit next-step block offering two or three options at different commitment levels, then lead or conversion rate from content traffic increases, because third-party evidence shows qualified readers bounce when the article ends with no direction.
ideas.run_when: Blog or guide traffic is a meaningful share of sessions and converts far below site average, with no consistent end-of-article CTA.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Content pages already end with a tested offer block, or the content is transactional rather than editorial.
ideas.plain_english: End articles with two or three clear next steps.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when blog or guide traffic is meaningful, converts far below site average, and ends with no CTA.

ideas.title: Collapse an interactive tool sitting above the CTA into an optional link
ideas.hypothesis: If an embedded interactive tool (delivery checker, calculator) above the buy button is collapsed to a text link, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows the widget absorbs attention and adds effort at the moment the CTA needs to flow.
ideas.run_when: An interactive widget sits between the price and the buy button, engagement with it is low, and heatmaps show attention pooling there.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The tool answers a blocking question for most buyers (for example a genuine fit or compatibility gate) or is a legal requirement.
ideas.plain_english: Collapse the interactive tool above the buy button into a small link.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when an interactive widget sits between price and buy button, engagement is low, and attention pools there.

ideas.title: Rebuild the pricing/plan page: trial terms, reassurance on fees and cancellation, highlighted best value
ideas.hypothesis: If the pricing page states what the buyer actually pays now, answers fee, contract and cancellation objections in place, and marks the best-value option, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows unresolved cost and commitment questions at the price step suppress selection.
ideas.run_when: There is a dedicated pricing, plan or bundle page with a measurable drop-off, and research lists cost ambiguity or commitment fear among the top objections.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Pricing is a single SKU with no plan choice, or the page has been rebuilt recently on the same research.
ideas.plain_english: Rebuild the pricing page: clear terms, fee answers, best value marked.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a pricing or plan page shows measurable drop off and research names cost ambiguity or commitment fear.

ideas.title: Add long-form sales copy ahead of the price or offer
ideas.hypothesis: If the page is expanded into a long-form argument that handles objections and anchors value before showing price, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows short pages ask for a decision before the visitor has enough information.
ideas.run_when: The offer is considered or unfamiliar, the current page is a short summary, and research shows unanswered objections at the buy decision.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Traffic is high-intent and already convinced, or the product is a low-consideration repeat purchase.
ideas.plain_english: Add a longer written argument before showing the price.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the offer is considered or unfamiliar, the page is short, and objections go unanswered.

ideas.title: Anchor-link index (Johnson box) auto-built from headings at the top of long information pages
ideas.hypothesis: If long information pages open with a linked index of their own headings, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows visitors rate dense information pages as overwhelming and abandon before reaching the section they need.
ideas.run_when: Long guide, spec or FAQ pages carry real traffic and score poorly on ease of use in research.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Pages are short enough to scan in one screen, or the index would push the primary content below the fold.
ideas.plain_english: Add a linked list of sections at the top of long pages.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when long guide, spec or FAQ pages carry traffic and score poorly on ease of use.

ideas.title: Strip upsells and value props from the add-to-cart confirmation modal, leaving product, total and two CTAs
ideas.hypothesis: If the add-to-cart modal is reduced to the product image, basket total and a continue-shopping / go-to-checkout pair, then checkout progression increases, because third-party evidence shows competing calls to action at that transition cause decision paralysis.
ideas.run_when: The ATC modal or cart drawer carries upsells, email capture and multiple value props, and drop-off between ATC and checkout start is above benchmark.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The drawer upsell is a verified AOV driver, or its removal would be measured on CVR alone without watching revenue per visitor.
ideas.plain_english: Strip the add to cart pop up back to product, total and two buttons.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the cart drawer carries upsells and email capture and add to cart to checkout drop off is above benchmark.

ideas.title: Consolidate duplicate sign-up or checkout entry flows into one
ideas.hypothesis: If scattered duplicate conversion entry points are consolidated into a single flow, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows fragmented journeys convert worse and split traffic across surfaces that can never be optimised properly.
ideas.run_when: The same conversion can start from two or more different forms or modals with different copy, and analytics show uneven performance between them.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The separate flows serve genuinely different audiences or offers with different qualifying data.
ideas.plain_english: Merge duplicate sign up or checkout flows into one.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the same conversion can start from two or more different forms with uneven performance.

ideas.title: Exit-intent modal on content pages carrying already-proven offer copy and imagery
ideas.hypothesis: If leaving content readers are shown an exit modal built from copy already proven on a converting page, then conversion rate increases, because third-party evidence shows content readers never see the commercial message and reused winning copy wins again on a new surface.
ideas.run_when: Article or guide traffic is large, converts poorly, and there is already a validated offer message from another surface to reuse.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Exit modals are already running on those pages, or the offer message has not been validated anywhere.
ideas.plain_english: Show leaving article readers a pop up using copy proven elsewhere.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when article traffic is large, converts poorly, and a validated offer message already exists elsewhere.

ideas.title: Recovery block on zero-results and dead-end pages
ideas.hypothesis: If zero-result searches and other dead-end pages show a recovery block (spelling suggestion, broader related products, and a best-sellers CTA) instead of an empty state, then site-wide conversion rate will increase, because searchers who reach a dead end currently have no path forward and exit.
ideas.run_when: Search or 404 pages carry meaningful session volume and site search analytics show a material zero-result rate.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Internal search volume is a trivial share of sessions.
ideas.plain_english: Give empty search and dead end pages a way forward.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when search or 404 pages carry real volume and site search shows a material zero result rate.

ideas.title: One-click post-purchase upsell before the confirmation page
ideas.hypothesis: If an upsell step appears after payment and before the confirmation page where the extra item is added with one click and no re-entry of payment details, then average order value will increase, because the buyer is at peak intent and the friction of a second purchase has been removed.
ideas.run_when: Checkout platform supports post-purchase offers without re-authorising payment, and there is a credible complementary or extra-quantity offer.
ideas.do_not_run_when: The offer would require the customer to re-enter payment or shipping details, or support load from combined-order confusion is already high.
ideas.plain_english: Offer a one click extra item after payment, before the confirmation page.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the platform supports post purchase offers without re authorising payment and a credible add on exists.

ideas.title: Popup timing and trigger rules
ideas.hypothesis: If entry popups are delayed, suppressed on high-intent pages, or moved to exit intent, then conversion rate will increase, because an interruption before the visitor has understood the offer costs more attention than the capture is worth.
ideas.run_when: An entry or timed popup fires early in the session on product or checkout paths.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Email capture is the primary business objective and list growth outweighs session conversion.
ideas.plain_english: Delay or suppress pop ups on the pages people buy from.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when an entry or timed pop up fires early on product or checkout paths.

ideas.title: Sitewide offer bar with a linked CTA
ideas.hypothesis: If the sitewide offer (free shipping, current promotion) is stated in a prominent top bar with a clickable CTA into the relevant collection, then revenue per visitor will increase, because the strongest commercial reason to buy is currently discoverable only by chance.
ideas.run_when: There is a genuine standing offer or shipping threshold and the current announcement bar is decorative or unlinked.
ideas.do_not_run_when: fabricated urgency
ideas.plain_english: Put the current offer in a top bar with a link to the products.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a genuine standing offer or shipping threshold exists but the announcement bar is decorative or unlinked.

ideas.title: Category labels in customer language
ideas.hypothesis: If navigation and subcategory labels are rewritten in the words customers use rather than internal or brand naming, then conversion rate will increase, because shoppers pick the wrong branch or none at all when a label does not describe what is behind it.
ideas.run_when: Site search and nav click data show shoppers bouncing between categories, or VOC shows different vocabulary from the menu.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Category names carry SEO ranking that would be lost, unless URLs and titles are held constant.
ideas.plain_english: Rename categories using the words customers actually use.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when nav click data shows shoppers bouncing between categories or research shows different vocabulary from the menu.

ideas.title: Sticky header carrying nav, search and cart
ideas.hypothesis: If the header with categories, search and the cart widget stays fixed while scrolling, then conversion rate will increase, because on long listing and product pages the way back into the funnel is otherwise a full scroll away.
ideas.run_when: Pages are long and scroll-depth data shows most engagement below the first viewport.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Mobile viewport is already crowded and the sticky bar would eat meaningful above-fold space.
ideas.plain_english: Keep the menu, search and cart fixed at the top while scrolling.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when pages are long and scroll data shows most engagement below the first viewport.

ideas.title: Autosuggest panel with products and categories
ideas.hypothesis: If the search field returns an autosuggest panel with matching products and categories (plus recent or trending queries before typing), then conversion rate will increase, because searchers convert at a higher rate than browsers and every query they abandon is a lost high-intent session.
ideas.run_when: Site search is used by a meaningful share of sessions and the catalogue is large enough that typing a full query is work.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Catalogue is tiny and browsing already surfaces everything.
ideas.plain_english: Show matching products and categories as people type in search.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when site search is used by a meaningful share of sessions and the catalogue is large.

ideas.title: Mini-cart contents, links and empty state
ideas.hypothesis: If the mini-cart shows items, quantity, discount and total with direct links to both cart and checkout (and a best-sellers prompt when empty), then checkout begin rate will increase, because shoppers can confirm what they are buying and start checkout without an extra page load.
ideas.run_when: Cart icon is a bare counter and analytics show drop-off between add-to-cart and cart view.
ideas.do_not_run_when: A cart drawer already performs this job.
ideas.plain_english: Show basket contents, totals and links in the mini cart.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the cart icon is a bare counter and analytics show drop off between add to cart and cart view.

ideas.title: Progress to the free-shipping threshold
ideas.hypothesis: If the cart and cart widget show how far the shopper is from the free-shipping threshold, and celebrate it once reached, then average order value will increase, because a stated gap turns an abstract threshold into a concrete, closable target.
ideas.run_when: A free-shipping threshold exists and a meaningful share of carts sit just below it.
ideas.do_not_run_when: No threshold exists, or margin cannot absorb the extra shipping at the threshold.
ideas.plain_english: Show shoppers how far they are from free shipping.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when a free shipping threshold exists and a meaningful share of carts sit just below it.

ideas.title: Founder story and proof of a real organisation
ideas.hypothesis: If the homepage carries the founders, the mission and visible proof of a real organisation (address, premises, faces), then conversion rate will increase, because first-time buyers on an unfamiliar D2C brand are deciding whether the company exists before they decide on the product.
ideas.run_when: High share of first-time visitors from paid traffic and low brand recognition.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Established brand where the story block only pushes product further down the page.
ideas.plain_english: Show the founders, the mission and proof the company is real.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when paid traffic brings mostly first time visitors and brand recognition is low.

ideas.title: Social follower and community counts
ideas.hypothesis: If follower and community counts are shown alongside social links, then conversion rate will increase, because a large visible audience is third-party evidence that the brand is real and used.
ideas.run_when: Follower counts are genuinely large for the category.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Counts are small enough to be counter-evidence, or the numbers cannot be stated accurately.
ideas.plain_english: Show follower and community numbers next to the social links.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only when follower counts are genuinely large for the category.

ideas.title: Visible way to ask a question at the decision points
ideas.hypothesis: If a visible contact route (chat, phone or email) sits at the product, cart and checkout decision points, then conversion rate will increase, because unanswered pre-purchase questions currently end the session rather than starting a conversation.
ideas.run_when: Considered or high-ticket purchase, and support volume shows recurring pre-purchase questions.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Nobody can staff the channel, since an unanswered chat widget damages trust more than its absence.
ideas.plain_english: Add a visible way to ask a question at the buying moments.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the purchase is considered or high ticket, support sees recurring pre purchase questions, and someone can staff it.

ideas.title: Press, award and known-brand logo strip
ideas.hypothesis: If genuine press mentions, awards and recognisable brand or retailer logos are shown near the top of the homepage and product page, then conversion rate will increase, because borrowed credibility answers the trust question faster than the brand's own claims.
ideas.run_when: Real, verifiable coverage or partnerships exist.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Logos would imply endorsement that was never given.
ideas.plain_english: Show genuine press, award and retailer logos near the top.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only where real, verifiable press coverage, awards or retail partnerships exist.

ideas.title: Customer photos of the product in use
ideas.hypothesis: If real customer photos showing the product in use (with faces and real settings) are placed on the product page, then conversion rate will increase, because shoppers judge fit and reality from other buyers' contexts, not studio shots.
ideas.run_when: UGC exists with rights to use it, and the product's value depends on how it looks or works in situ.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Only low-quality or unlicensed images are available.
ideas.plain_english: Show real customer photos of the product being used.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when licensed customer photos exist and the product's value depends on how it looks in place.

ideas.title: Default sort order and the sort control
ideas.hypothesis: If collections default to best-selling or top-rated products and the sort control is visible above the grid, then revenue per visitor will increase, because the first row does most of the work and a manual-ordered or arbitrary default wastes it.
ideas.run_when: Collections hold enough products that ordering matters and current default is manual or by date.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Collection is curated deliberately for merchandising or seasonal reasons.
ideas.plain_english: Default collections to best selling and show the sort control.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when collections hold enough products that ordering matters and the default is manual or by date.

ideas.title: Second product image on hover or swipe
ideas.hypothesis: If listing cards reveal a second image on hover (or swipe on mobile), then conversion rate will increase, because shoppers can rule products in or out on the listing instead of paying a page load to find out.
ideas.run_when: Products are visually differentiated and a strong alternate angle or in-use shot exists for most SKUs.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Image library is inconsistent, so the second shot varies wildly in quality between products.
ideas.plain_english: Show a second product image on hover or swipe.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when products are visually differentiated and a strong second shot exists for most items.

ideas.title: Available variants shown on the listing card
ideas.hypothesis: If listing cards show which colours and sizes are actually available, then conversion rate will increase, because shoppers currently open product pages only to discover their variant is missing, and abandon rather than return.
ideas.run_when: Products carry multiple variants and stock-outs at variant level are common.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Nearly all products are single-variant.
ideas.plain_english: Show which colours and sizes are in stock on the listing card.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when products carry multiple variants and variant level stock outs are common.

ideas.title: Low-stock and sold-out labelling
ideas.hypothesis: If genuine low-stock counts are shown on cards, product pages and cart lines, with sold-out items still visible, then conversion rate will increase, because a real and verifiable limit converts deferred decisions into decisions now.
ideas.run_when: Inventory data is accurate and live, and stock genuinely runs low on some SKUs.
ideas.do_not_run_when: fabricated urgency
ideas.plain_english: Show genuine low stock counts and keep sold out items visible.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only when inventory data is accurate and live and stock genuinely runs low.

ideas.title: Back-in-stock email capture on sold-out products
ideas.hypothesis: If sold-out products offer a back-in-stock email capture in place of a dead add-to-cart, then revenue will increase, because demand that currently exits with nothing is captured and returned to when stock lands.
ideas.run_when: Stock-outs are frequent, restocks are reliable, and the notification email actually sends.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Products are discontinued rather than restocked, which makes the promise a broken one.
ideas.plain_english: Let shoppers ask to be told when a sold out product returns.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when stock outs are frequent, restocks are reliable, and the notification email actually sends.

ideas.title: Easy zoom on the main product image
ideas.hypothesis: If the main product image supports easy zoom, particularly on mobile, then add-to-cart rate will increase, because material, texture and finish decide the purchase and cannot be judged at thumbnail scale.
ideas.run_when: Product quality is visible in detail (texture, stitching, finish) and source images are high resolution.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Image assets are low resolution, where zoom exposes rather than reassures.
ideas.plain_english: Let shoppers zoom into the main product image easily.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when quality shows in detail and source images are high resolution, especially for mobile.

ideas.title: Gallery follows the selected variant
ideas.hypothesis: If selecting a colour or size swaps the gallery to images of that exact variant, then add-to-cart rate will increase, because shoppers will not commit to a variant they have not seen.
ideas.run_when: Variants differ visually and per-variant imagery exists.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Only one photo set exists across variants, which would make the switch misleading.
ideas.plain_english: Switch the photos to match the colour or size selected.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when variants differ visually and per variant imagery already exists.

ideas.title: Reminder when add-to-cart is pressed without a variant
ideas.hypothesis: If pressing add-to-cart without a size or colour selected triggers a visible, adjacent reminder rather than a silent failure or a generic error, then add-to-cart rate will increase, because the shopper intended to buy and lost the thread at a recoverable step.
ideas.run_when: Products require variant selection and event data shows add-to-cart clicks that produce no cart event.
ideas.do_not_run_when: A recommended variant is preselected, so the failure state does not occur.
ideas.plain_english: Show a clear reminder when someone adds to cart without picking a size.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when products need a variant chosen and event data shows add to cart clicks producing no cart event.

ideas.title: Inline variant and quantity selectors instead of dropdowns
ideas.hypothesis: If variants and quantity use visible inline selectors that update price and imagery without a page reload, instead of dropdowns, then add-to-cart rate will increase, because the options and their consequences become visible rather than hidden behind a click.
ideas.run_when: Option counts are small enough to display inline and the theme currently uses dropdowns or reloads.
ideas.do_not_run_when: There are dozens of options, where inline display becomes a wall of controls.
ideas.plain_english: Show variants and quantity as visible buttons instead of dropdowns.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when option counts are small and the theme currently uses dropdowns or page reloads.

ideas.title: Measurements in the visitor's own units
ideas.hypothesis: If dimensions and weights are shown in the units of the visitor's market (or both sets side by side), then conversion rate will increase, because a shopper who has to convert measurements to check fit often leaves to do the maths and does not come back.
ideas.run_when: Meaningful traffic from markets on a different measurement system and fit or size matters.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Single-market store where the units are already native.
ideas.plain_english: Show sizes and weights in the visitor's own units.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when meaningful traffic comes from markets on a different measurement system and fit matters.

ideas.title: Confirmation state after add-to-cart
ideas.hypothesis: If adding to cart produces an unmistakable confirmation (button state change, then a prompt onward to the cart) rather than only a counter increment, then checkout begin rate will increase, because shoppers who cannot tell whether the add worked either re-add or stall.
ideas.run_when: Current feedback is a small cart-count change, and replay shows repeated add-to-cart clicks.
ideas.do_not_run_when: A cart drawer already opens on add, since the confirmation is then already unmissable.
ideas.plain_english: Give a clear confirmation when something is added to the cart.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run when the only feedback is a small cart count change and replay shows repeated add to cart clicks.

ideas.title: Was-price strikethrough with the saving stated
ideas.hypothesis: If discounted products show the old price struck through alongside the new price and the saving stated in currency or percent (and the cart totals the saving), then revenue per visitor will increase, because a discount the shopper has to calculate is a discount they do not feel.
ideas.run_when: Genuine prior prices exist and the discount is real and compliant with local pricing law.
ideas.do_not_run_when: There is no genuine prior selling price to reference.
ideas.plain_english: Show the old price struck through with the saving stated.
ideas.ideation_hint: Run only where genuine prior prices exist and the discount complies with local pricing law.

ideas.title: Express payment buttons at the buy decision
ideas.hypothesis: If express wallet buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Shop Pay) sit beside or below the main CTA on the product page and cart, then conversion rate will increase, because the whole address and card entry step disappears for buyers who already have a wallet.
ideas.run_when: Wallet share of payments is meaningful and mobile traffic dominates.
ideas.do_not_run_when: Express checkout bypasses steps the store needs (upsells, delivery options, order attributes), or the buttons would push the price and CTA below the fold.
